description: The Global Energy Ownership Tracker from Global Energy Monitor (GEM), a non-profit research organisation, maps who ultimately owns key energy assets, from the direct owner of each project up to the ultimate parents, such as corporations, investment firms and governments. On 26 September 2026 the page counted more than 27,000 entities, 25,000 ownership relationships and 31,000 assets. Links carry ownership percentages, including minority stakes above 5%, for assets in nine GEM trackers: coal plants, oil and gas plants, coal mines, iron and steel, bioenergy plants, iron ore mines, gas transmission pipelines, oil and NGL pipelines, and cement and concrete. Beta tools explore ownership trees, portfolios and asset classes. The data are updated after each release of the underlying trackers; the latest was September 2026. Coverage is global. Access is through a free online tracker map, dashboards and summary tables, and the full data set is a spreadsheet downloadable through a short download form on GEM's site, under CC BY 4.0 at no cost. Caveats: ownership chains are researched from public filings and may be incomplete for private owners. Simulation uses are concentration and counterparty risk analysis of energy assets and linking operators across interdependent systems. Related records: data-gem-global-integrated-power-tracker and the other GEM trackers hold the assets.
